body:
This fix isn't entirely correct. If you completely remove the check for abstract functions, you should probably remove it for non-abstract functions as well, if everything works correctly.

However, I think the check here should be corrected so that it takes into account not only the presence of `return` in the function body (`p_func->body->has_return`), but also the declared return type (`p_func->return_type`), which shouldn't be equal to `nullptr` or a `TypeNode *` that represents the GDScript type `void`.

The GDScript analyzer attempts to take into account not only the declared function type but also partially infers it from the `return` uses in the function body. Although it doesn't do this entirely correctly, I've seen several bugs (probably because we don't distinguish between void return and non-void return). However, this is probably beyond the scope of this PR.

Our mistake was that when adding abstract functions, we forgot to check for conditions involving the function body, which abstract functions lack (but use empty stubs as bodies to prevent crashes). I can recall at least one example in the doc generator. It's possible that everything here is correct, but it's worth making sure.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6e4e8072e1daabc85ea6bd6b8178aad7004eaef0/modules/gdscript/editor/gdscript_docgen.cpp#L441-L444

Also, you should add test cases to `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/runtime/features/member_info.gd` or `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/runtime/features/member_info_inheritance.gd` to ensure the correctness of the provided `MethodInfo` and avoid possible regressions in the future.

@dalexeev 
After consider about the logic of previous codes, I checked  both `p_func->body->has_return` and `p_func->return_type`. When there is an explicity return_type declaration, I will use it as return_type directly. When there is no `return_type` declaration, we will go further to check whether there is any `return` in the function body, if there is no return phase, we will use `void`, besides `variant`.

I updated the `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/runtime/features/member_info_inheritance.gd` and confirmed the result is compliant as before, and when there are return_type declared in abstract method, we can get correct return_type. But the member_info.out didn't show the difference, do you give me some clue for it?

And there is still a confusion on abstract method without explicity return type. In current codes, we have three situations:

1. If there is a return type declaration, we use it.
2. If there is not a return type declaration, and there is return phrase in body, we return variant as return type.
3. No return type declaration, and no return phrase in body, return void.

If we have a abstract method without explicity return type declaration, should it return void or variant? Because abstract method has no body, maybe the override method of child class can have a return phrase?
